report.summary: Chunk 2 of 5: PlainNaming, _py_dotted, types_by_file, TypeGraph, _Resolver with methods for naming, views, bindings, and candidate generation.
risks: PlainNaming.from_rels | medium | Ambiguity handling: when multiple real (non-.pyi) candidates exist, the method silently ignores them (no entry in rel_by_dotted). This could lead to unresolved names later. To settle: verify that callers handle missing dotted names gracefully.

_Resolver._view | medium | The view construction merges importer and its imports, but if a dotted name maps to multiple rels (e.g., both pkg/__init__.py and pkg.py), the view excludes that name entirely (len(set(rels)) != 1). This may cause false negatives for types from such modules. To settle: check if such collisions are common and if the design intentionally refuses them.

_Resolver._bare_candidates | medium | When a name is bound from a module not in the view (rel is None), the candidate list remains empty even if the binding exists. This may lead to unresolved outcomes for valid imports. To settle: confirm that the caller handles this case correctly (e.g., falls back to external resolution).

handoff.purpose: Defines PlainNaming, types_by_file, TypeGraph, and _Resolver infrastructure for type resolution.

claims.why: The rule is implemented in this chunk (stem = rel[:-3] if .py else rsplit('.',1)[0], then replace '/', '.'). The claim that it is the same as index._py_dotted cannot be verified because index._py_dotted is not in this chunk.

claims.text: It is never merged into ``graph.SymbolResolver.defs_by_file`` and never passed to ``graph.build_resolver``.
claims.why: The function types_by_file is defined, but its usage relative to graph.SymbolResolver is not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: Keyed by the full in-file ``qualname`` (``Outer.Inner``, not ``Inner``), because a leaf-name key would make two nested classes with the same leaf name collide and force a tie-break.
claims.why: The code uses decl.qualname as key in bucket, which is the full qualified name.

claims.text: A qualname declared twice in one file (an ``if``/``try`` pair) keeps the FIRST by line: both spellings share one node id, so there is nothing to arbitrate. The count is published as ``duplicate_declarations``.
claims.why: The code uses bucket.setdefault(decl.qualname, decl) which keeps the first occurrence. The claim about sharing one node id and duplicate_declarations count cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: ``nodes`` is sorted by id. ``edges`` maps every relation name in ``RELATIONS`` (always present, possibly empty) to a tuple of ``{"source", "target", "attributes"}`` rows sorted by ``(source, target, canonical attributes)``.
claims.why: The class definition shows fields but no logic enforcing sorting or the structure of edges. The claim about sorting and RELATIONS cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: Stage 3 publishes these verbatim under a ``types_on`` gate. The ``excluded_from`` list is spelled out for the same reason the documents block spells out its own: a consumer who sees a type layer in the index and zero type nodes in ``hotspots`` must be able to read WHY here instead of inferring a clean bill of health.
claims.why: The method returns a dict, but the claim about stage 3, types_on gate, and consumer behavior cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: Constructed AFTER every declaration in the repo is registered, so it is two-pass by construction and a forward reference is not a special case.
claims.why: The __init__ method is defined, but the claim about when it is constructed relative to declaration registration cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: This is the "reuse the import edges, do not recompute them" step. The candidate set is the file's own import targets (plus itself), so a resolved type edge always sits on top of an import edge that ``index.py`` already published; a module this file does not import cannot supply a type to it even if the dotted name would match.
claims.why: The code builds by_name from importer and self._imports.get(importer, ()), and only includes rels present in self._facts. The view only contains dotted names with exactly one rel, so the claim about reusing import edges is consistent with the code.

claims.text: Relative levels are anchored exactly the way ``parse.resolve_python_imports`` anchors them, so the two never disagree about which package a ``from ..x import y`` means.
claims.why: The method implements relative level anchoring using self._dotted(importer) and splitting. The claim that it matches parse.resolve_python_imports cannot be verified because that function is not in this chunk.

claims.text: The membership test is the ONLY thing that mints a target: a name is never minted into a node for having been mentioned.
claims.why: The method returns the node id only if qualname in self._tbf.get(rel, {}), i.e., only if declared. It does not create nodes otherwise.

claims.text: Two bindings that AGREE (the common ``if TYPE_CHECKING`` duplicate) are not a disagreement and still resolve.
claims.why: The method collects targets from bindings and uses them later (not shown in this chunk). The claim about agreement resolving cannot be fully verified because the resolution logic after _bare_candidates is not in this chunk.

observations.what: PlainNaming.from_rels does not handle the case where multiple real (non-.pyi) candidates exist for the same dotted name; it simply omits the entry. This may cause later lookups to fail silently.
types_by_file uses setdefault to keep the first declaration, but the docstring mentions 'duplicate_declarations' count which is not present in this chunk.

_Resolver._view includes the importer itself and its imports, but if a dotted name maps to multiple rels (e.g., both pkg/__init__.py and pkg.py), the view excludes that name entirely. This could cause types from such modules to be unresolved even if one is the intended target.

_Resolver._bare_candidates returns an empty list when the binding's module is not in the view (rel is None), even if the binding exists. This may lead to false UNRESOLVED outcomes for valid external imports.
